name: Hegmataneh
description: Hegmataneh is the buried hill-top city beneath modern Hamadan, in the Zagros Mountains of northwestern Iran. It was the capital of the Medes in the 7th and 6th centuries BCE, widely regarded as Iran's first capital. Later Persian, Greek, Parthian and Sasanian rulers escaped the lowland heat here each summer, and people have lived on the site for nearly three thousand years.
